questions.q: The imaginary line at 0° latitude that divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres is called the ______.
questions.e: The Equator is the 0° line of latitude, midway between the two poles.

questions.q: The Prime Meridian (0° longitude) passes through which place in England?
questions.e: By international agreement, the meridian passing through Greenwich near London is taken as 0° longitude.

questions.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.e: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of the Earth's surface.

questions.q: Which is the largest continent by area?
questions.e: Asia is the largest continent both in area and population.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain peak in the world?
questions.e: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha in Nepal, Chomolungma in Tibet) in the Himalayas is the world's highest peak.

questions.t: History: Timeline and Sources of History
questions.q: Scientists who study the past by digging up and examining material remains such as tools, pottery and buildings are called ______.
questions.e: Archaeologists excavate and study material remains to reconstruct the past.

questions.t: History: Timeline and Sources of History
questions.q: How many years make one century?
questions.e: A century is a period of 100 years.

questions.q: Article 1 of the Constitution says: 'India, that is ______, shall be a Union of States.'
questions.e: Article 1 of the Constitution names the country as 'India, that is Bharat'.

questions.t: History: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation
questions.q: Which Harappan city, now in Pakistan, is famous for the Great Bath?
questions.e: The Great Bath, a large watertight tank, was found in the citadel of Mohenjo-daro.

questions.q: Which is the oldest of the four Vedas?
questions.e: The Rig Veda is the oldest of the four Vedas and among the oldest texts in the world.

questions.q: The elected head of a Gram Panchayat is commonly called the ______.
questions.e: The Gram Panchayat is headed by an elected Sarpanch, also called Pradhan or Mukhiya in some states.

questions.q: Who wrote India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.e: Jana Gana Mana was composed by Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.q: Activities done in exchange for money, or that produce goods and services of monetary value, are called ______ activities.
questions.e: Economic activities earn money or create goods and services that have monetary value.

questions.q: Farming, fishing and mining belong to which sector of economic activity?
questions.e: The primary sector takes resources directly from nature.

questions.q: Which important line of latitude passes almost through the middle of India?
questions.e: The Tropic of Cancer (about 23.5°N) runs through states such as Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal.

questions.q: In ancient India, the prime meridian was taken to pass through which city, a famous centre of astronomy?
questions.e: Indian astronomers used a 'madhya rekha' (central line) passing through Ujjain as their prime meridian.

questions.q: Which is the only ocean named after a country?
questions.e: The Indian Ocean is named after India.

questions.q: A large, mostly flat raised area of land that rises sharply above the surrounding area is called a ______.
questions.e: A plateau is an elevated flat-topped land, like the Deccan plateau.

questions.q: The name 'India' comes from the river Indus, which in Sanskrit is called the ______.
questions.e: Persians and Greeks adapted 'Sindhu' into 'Hindu' and 'Indos', which gave the name India.

questions.t: History: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation
questions.q: Which Harappan site in Gujarat is known for its dockyard?
questions.e: Lothal had a large basin interpreted as a dockyard, showing sea trade.

questions.q: At which place did the Buddha deliver his first sermon?
questions.e: The Buddha gave his first sermon at the deer park in Sarnath near Varanasi.

questions.q: The body made up of all adult voters of a village, which meets to discuss local issues, is called the ______.
questions.e: The Gram Sabha includes every adult voter of the village and oversees the Gram Panchayat.

questions.q: Which of the three organs of government makes laws?
questions.e: The legislature makes laws, the executive implements them and the judiciary interprets them.

questions.q: In a city, each area that elects a councillor to the municipal body is called a ______.
questions.e: A city is divided into wards, each electing a ward councillor.

questions.q: Who is the head of a Municipal Corporation in a large city?
questions.e: A Municipal Corporation is headed by a Mayor.

questions.q: Bihu is a harvest festival celebrated mainly in which state?
questions.e: Bihu marks the agricultural seasons of Assam.

questions.q: A doctor treating patients free of cost at a relief camp, as a volunteer, is doing a ______ activity.
questions.e: Work done without expecting payment, out of care or service, is a non-economic activity.

questions.q: Which Sanskrit word, used in the new NCERT book, means selfless service to others without expecting any reward?
questions.e: Seva means selfless service done for the good of others.

questions.q: Money received by a worker in exchange for work done is called ______.
questions.e: Workers are paid wages or salary as the monetary value of their work.

questions.q: Banking, transport, teaching and healthcare belong to which sector?
questions.e: The tertiary or service sector provides services rather than goods.

questions.q: The Earth rotates through 360° of longitude in 24 hours. How many degrees of longitude does it turn through in one hour?
questions.e: 360 ÷ 24 = 15, so the Earth turns 15° every hour.

questions.q: A ship sails west from India, crosses the Arabian Sea, rounds the southern tip of Africa and continues north-west to Brazil. Which ocean does it cross last?
questions.e: The Atlantic Ocean lies between Africa and South America.

questions.q: Most of India's densely populated regions lie on river plains. Which type of soil, deposited by rivers, makes these plains so fertile?
questions.e: Rivers deposit fine fertile alluvium, which supports intensive farming and dense settlement.

questions.t: History: Timeline and Sources of History
questions.q: A king ruled from 320 BCE to 298 BCE. For how many years did he rule?
questions.e: BCE years count backwards, so 320 - 298 = 22 years.

questions.t: History: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation
questions.q: Harappan seals have been found in distant Mesopotamia. What does this mainly indicate about the Harappans?
questions.a: Long-distance trade|Trade|Foreign trade|Overseas trade|Long distance trade
questions.e: Harappan objects in Mesopotamia show that the two regions traded with each other.

questions.q: The Jain idea that truth has many sides and no single viewpoint holds the complete truth is called ______.
questions.e: Anekantavada teaches respect for many points of view.

questions.q: Arrange the three tiers of Panchayati Raj from the village level upward.
questions.a: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad
o: Zila Parishad, Panchayat Samiti, Gram Panchayat
Panchayat Samiti, Gram Panchayat, Zila Parishad
Gram Panchayat, Zila Parishad, Panchayat Samiti
questions.e: Gram Panchayat works at village level, Panchayat Samiti at block level and Zila Parishad at district level.

questions.q: A democracy in which citizens elect people to make decisions on their behalf is called ______ democracy.
questions.e: In representative democracy, elected representatives make laws and decisions for the people.

questions.q: Pongal, Lohri, Onam and Bihu are celebrated in different states, yet they share one common theme. What is it?
questions.e: All four are harvest festivals, showing unity in diversity in how Indians celebrate farming.

questions.q: Rekha runs a tea stall and also cooks meals at home for her family. Which of these two activities is an economic activity?
questions.a: Running the tea stall|Tea stall|The tea stall|Running a tea stall
questions.e: Selling tea earns money, while cooking for the family is unpaid household work.

questions.q: A farmer grows cotton, a mill turns it into cloth and a shop sells the cloth. The mill's activity belongs to which sector?
questions.e: Turning raw materials into finished goods is manufacturing, part of the secondary sector.

questions.q: Which of the following sequences correctly shows the journey of a cotton shirt from field to buyer?
questions.e: Cotton is grown (primary), made into a shirt (secondary) and sold in a shop (tertiary).

questions.q: Assertion (A): India has been known by many names such as Bharata, Hindustan and India. Reason (R): Different peoples, including Indians, Persians and Greeks, named the land in their own languages.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R explains A
o: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Each name arose from a different language tradition, so R correctly explains A.

questions.q: Which of the following is an economic activity?
questions.a: A tailor stitching clothes for customers
o: A mother cooking for her family
A student helping a friend study
questions.e: The tailor earns money for the work; the others are unpaid non-economic activities.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches a landform with an Indian example?
questions.e: The Deccan is a plateau; the Aravallis are mountains, Thar is a desert and the Ganga basin is a plain.

questions.t: History: The Beginnings of Indian Civilisation
questions.q: Passage: Mohenjo-daro had streets laid out in a grid, houses built of baked bricks and covered drains. In its citadel stood a large tank with steps on two sides, made watertight with a layer of natural tar.
p: (a) What is this large tank commonly called?
Great Bath|The Great Bath
(b) What natural tar-like material made the tank watertight?
Bitumen|Natural tar
(c) What kind of bricks were used for most of the buildings?
Baked bricks|Burnt bricks|Fired bricks|Kiln-fired bricks
questions.e: The Great Bath used baked bricks sealed with bitumen, showing advanced Harappan building skills.

questions.q: India stretches from about 68°E to 97°E longitude. The Earth turns 1° of longitude every 4 minutes.
p: (a) What is the difference in degrees between 97°E and 68°E?
degrees
(b) What is the local time difference, in minutes, between these two longitudes?
minutes
questions.e: 97 - 68 = 29°, and 29 × 4 = 116 minutes, nearly two hours, which is why India uses one standard time.

questions.q: Rani's village elects a Gram Panchayat, and its Gram Sabha meets regularly. Her uncle lives in a large city governed by a Municipal Corporation.
p: (a) What is the elected representative of a city ward called?
Councillor|Ward councillor|Corporator|Municipal councillor
(b) Which constitutional amendment of 1992 gave Panchayati Raj institutions constitutional status? Give its number.
questions.e: Cities elect ward councillors, and the 73rd Amendment (1992) made Panchayati Raj a constitutional system.

questions.q: Siddhartha Gautama left his palace in search of the causes of human suffering. After long meditation under a pipal tree, he attained enlightenment.
p: (a) At which place did he attain enlightenment?
Bodh Gaya|Bodhgaya|Gaya
(b) By what title did he become known after enlightenment?
Buddha|The Buddha|Enlightened One
(c) Which teacher of the same period is regarded as the 24th tirthankara of Jainism?
Mahavira|Vardhamana|Vardhamana Mahavira
questions.e: Siddhartha became the Buddha at Bodh Gaya; his contemporary Mahavira was the 24th Jain tirthankara.

questions.q: Data: In a village of 100 workers, 60 people farm, 25 work in a brick kiln and a sugar mill, and 15 run shops, transport services and a school.
p: (a) How many workers are in the tertiary sector?
workers
(b) What percentage of the workers are in the primary sector?
(c) In which sector do the brick kiln and sugar mill workers work?
Secondary sector|Secondary|Manufacturing
questions.e: Farming is primary, kiln and mill work is secondary, and shops, transport and schools are tertiary.

questions.q: The word 'Himalaya' means 'abode of ______'.
questions.e: In Sanskrit, hima means snow and alaya means abode.

questions.q: Which large desert lies mainly in western Rajasthan?
questions.e: The Thar or Great Indian Desert covers much of western Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which instrument measures air temperature?
questions.e: A thermometer measures how hot or cold the air is.

questions.q: The seasonal winds that bring most of India's rainfall are called the ______.
questions.e: The south-west monsoon winds bring most of India's annual rain from June to September.

questions.t: History: New Beginnings: Cities and States
questions.q: The sixteen large kingdoms of ancient India around the 6th century BCE, the 'great janapadas', are called ______.
questions.e: Mahajanapada means 'great janapada'; texts list sixteen of them.

questions.q: Who founded the Maurya Empire?
questions.e: Chandragupta Maurya, guided by Chanakya, founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE.

questions.q: Who founded the Shunga dynasty after overthrowing the last Mauryan ruler?
questions.e: Pushyamitra Shunga, a Mauryan general, founded the Shunga dynasty.

questions.q: Which Gupta-era mathematician and astronomer wrote the Aryabhatiya?
questions.e: Aryabhata wrote the Aryabhatiya and stated that the Earth rotates on its axis.

questions.q: A system in which a king or queen rules and power usually passes within a family is called a ______.
questions.e: In a monarchy, rule is usually hereditary.

questions.q: Who was the chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?
questions.a: B. R. Ambedkar|B.R. Ambedkar|BR Ambedkar|Ambedkar|Bhimrao Ambedkar|Babasaheb Ambedkar|Dr Ambedkar
questions.e: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

questions.q: On which date did the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.e: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.q: The direct exchange of goods for goods without using money is called ______.
questions.e: In barter, goods or services are exchanged directly for other goods or services.

questions.q: Small sea shells once used as money in many parts of India and the world were called ______.
questions.e: Cowrie shells were widely used as small change in India for centuries.

questions.q: A weekly market held on a fixed day in villages and small towns is commonly called a ______.
questions.e: Weekly haats bring sellers and buyers together on a fixed day.

questions.q: The Western Ghats are also known by which name in Maharashtra and Karnataka?
questions.e: The northern Western Ghats are called the Sahyadri.

questions.q: The Lakshadweep islands are mainly made up of what?
questions.e: Lakshadweep is a group of coral islands in the Arabian Sea.

questions.q: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
questions.e: A barometer measures air pressure; falling pressure often signals stormy weather.

questions.q: The amount of water vapour present in the air is called ______.
questions.e: Humidity is the moisture content of the air, measured with a hygrometer.

questions.q: Which hot, dry and dusty wind blows over the plains of north India on summer afternoons?
questions.e: The Loo is a hot, dry summer wind of north and north-west India.

questions.t: History: New Beginnings: Cities and States
questions.q: Vaishali was the capital of which famous gana-sangha (republic)?
questions.e: The Vajji confederacy, led by the Licchavis, was ruled by an assembly and had its capital at Vaishali.

questions.q: Which Mauryan emperor gave up war after the Kalinga war and spread the idea of dhamma?
questions.e: Ashoka was moved by the suffering of the Kalinga war and turned to dhamma.

questions.q: The Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft and economy, is traditionally attributed to whom?
questions.e: Kautilya, also called Chanakya, adviser to Chandragupta Maurya, is credited with the Arthashastra.

questions.q: The Hathigumpha inscription describes the achievements of which king of Kalinga?
questions.e: The Hathigumpha inscription near Bhubaneswar records the deeds of King Kharavela.

questions.q: Which Sanskrit poet and playwright of the Gupta period wrote 'Abhijnanashakuntalam'?
questions.e: Kalidasa wrote Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta and other classics.

questions.q: Rule by a small group of powerful or wealthy people is called ______.
questions.e: Oligarchy means rule by a few.

questions.q: A government run by religious leaders according to religious law is called a ______.
questions.e: In a theocracy, religious authorities hold political power.

questions.q: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed on 26 November because on this day in 1949 the Constitution was ______.
questions.e: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949.

questions.q: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: Dr Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly and later became India's first President.

questions.q: Barter works only when each person wants what the other has. This requirement is called the '______ of wants'.
questions.e: Without a double coincidence of wants, barter cannot take place.

questions.q: The earliest coins of India, mostly of silver with symbols stamped on them, are called ______ coins.
questions.e: Punch-marked coins had symbols punched onto silver pieces.

questions.q: The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove delta, is formed by which two rivers together?
questions.a: Ganga and Brahmaputra|Ganga-Brahmaputra|Brahmaputra and Ganga|Ganga Brahmaputra
questions.e: The Ganga and Brahmaputra together build the Sundarbans delta.

questions.q: Weather is the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere. What term describes the average weather of a place over about 30 years or more?
questions.e: Climate is the long-term pattern of weather in a region.

questions.q: Coastal Tamil Nadu gets much of its rain in October–December, when most of India is dry. Which winds bring this rain?
questions.a: Northeast monsoon|North-east monsoon|Retreating monsoon|Northeast monsoon winds
questions.e: The retreating north-east monsoon picks up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and rains on the Tamil Nadu coast.

questions.t: History: New Beginnings: Cities and States
questions.q: Which mahajanapada became the most powerful, helped by fertile land, iron ore deposits, rivers and strong rulers?
questions.e: Magadha's resources and able rulers made it the foundation of later empires.

questions.q: The Greek ambassador Megasthenes described the Mauryan capital in his book 'Indica'. Which city was it?
questions.e: Pataliputra, near modern Patna, was the Mauryan capital.

questions.q: The Kushana king Kanishka controlled part of a great trade network linking China, Central Asia and the Roman world. What was this network called?
questions.e: Silk and other goods moved across Asia along the Silk Road, and the Kushanas profited from it.

questions.q: The rust-resistant iron pillar from the Gupta age, showing advanced metallurgy, now stands in which city?
questions.e: The iron pillar in the Qutb complex, Mehrauli, Delhi, has resisted rust for over 1,500 years.

questions.q: A country where the head of state is elected and is not a hereditary monarch is called a ______.
questions.e: India is a republic because its President is elected.

questions.q: The introductory statement of the Constitution that sets out its ideals and objectives is called the ______.
questions.e: The Preamble begins 'We, the People of India' and states the Constitution's ideals.

questions.q: Under universal adult franchise, citizens of what minimum age can vote in India?
questions.e: Every citizen aged 18 or above can vote, whatever their caste, gender, religion or wealth.

questions.q: Which of the following is the main reason money replaced barter?
questions.a: It removed the need for a double coincidence of wants
o: It was heavier to carry than goods
questions.e: Money is accepted by everyone, so traders no longer need to find someone who wants exactly their goods.

questions.q: When many sellers offer the same product and compete for buyers, what usually happens to its price?
questions.e: Competition among sellers pushes prices down.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of democracy but NOT of a dictatorship?
o: Rulers cannot be removed by the people
questions.e: Only a democracy lets people choose and change their rulers through free elections.

questions.q: Arrange these forms of exchange in the order they appeared in history.
questions.a: Barter, metal coins, paper notes, digital payments
o: Metal coins, barter, paper notes, digital payments
Barter, paper notes, metal coins, digital payments
Paper notes, barter, digital payments, metal coins
questions.e: Barter came first, then coins, then paper currency, and most recently digital payments such as UPI.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The price of tomatoes usually falls when there is a very large harvest. Reason (R): When supply increases while demand stays the same, prices tend to fall.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R explains A
o: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: A big harvest raises supply, and with unchanged demand the price falls, so R explains A.

questions.q: Data: Rainfall recorded at a school weather station over one week (mm): Mon 12, Tue 0, Wed 8, Thu 20, Fri 0, Sat 5, Sun 4.
p: (a) What was the total rainfall for the week?
mm
(b) What was the average daily rainfall?
mm
(c) Which instrument is used to measure rainfall?
Rain gauge|Raingauge|Rain gage
questions.e: 12+0+8+20+0+5+4 = 49 mm and 49 ÷ 7 = 7 mm; rainfall is measured with a rain gauge.

questions.q: Passage: The Prayagraj (Allahabad) pillar inscription, composed by the court poet Harishena, praises a Gupta king for his many conquests and also for his skill in music and poetry.
p: (a) Which Gupta king does this inscription praise?
Samudragupta
(b) In which language was this praise-poem (prashasti) composed?
Sanskrit
questions.e: Harishena's Sanskrit prashasti on the Prayagraj pillar celebrates Samudragupta.

questions.q: The Preamble declares India to be a 'Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic'.
p: (a) Which word means the state does not favour any one religion?
Secular
(b) Which word means India makes its own decisions without outside control?
Sovereign
(c) Which word means people elect their government and leaders?
Democratic|Democracy
questions.e: Each word of the Preamble expresses a core value of the Indian state.

questions.q: A potter has 10 pots and wants rice. A farmer has rice but wants cloth, not pots.
p: (a) Can a direct barter take place between the potter and the farmer? (Yes/No)
No
(b) If the farmer later agreed that 1 pot = 2 kg of rice, how many kg of rice would 10 pots fetch?
kg
questions.e: Barter fails without a double coincidence of wants; if agreed, 10 × 2 = 20 kg.

questions.q: A wholesaler buys 100 kg of onions from farmers at ₹20 per kg and sells them to a retailer at ₹25 per kg. The retailer sells to customers at ₹30 per kg.
p: (a) What is the wholesaler's total profit on the 100 kg?
(b) A person who buys goods for their own use, such as a family buying onions, is called a ______.
Consumer|Customer|Buyer
questions.e: Profit = 100 × (25 - 20) = ₹500; the final buyer is the consumer.

questions.t: Geography: Natural Resources and Their Use
questions.q: Resources that are replenished naturally, such as sunlight and wind, are called ______ resources.
questions.e: Renewable resources are renewed by natural processes.

questions.t: Geography: Natural Resources and Their Use
questions.q: Collecting and storing rainwater from rooftops to use it or recharge groundwater is called ______.
questions.e: Rainwater harvesting captures rain that would otherwise run off.

questions.q: Crops sown with the onset of the monsoon and harvested in autumn, such as rice and cotton, are called ______ crops.
questions.e: Kharif crops grow during the rainy season.

questions.q: Which city is known as the 'Silicon Valley of India' for its information technology industry?
questions.e: Bengaluru is India's leading IT hub.

questions.q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India after winning the First Battle of Panipat?
questions.e: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526 and founded Mughal rule.

questions.t: History: The Rise of the Marathas
questions.q: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 at which fort?
questions.e: Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad fort in 1674.

questions.t: History: The Rise of the Marathas
questions.q: Shivaji's council of eight ministers was called the ______.
questions.e: The Ashtapradhan was a council of eight ministers who helped Shivaji run the state.

questions.t: History: The Colonial Era in India
questions.q: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
questions.e: In 1757 Robert Clive's forces defeated Siraj-ud-daulah at Plassey.

questions.t: Civics: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
questions.q: Which constitutional body conducts elections to Parliament and the state legislatures in India?
questions.e: The Election Commission of India conducts free and fair elections under Article 324.

questions.q: The lower house of India's Parliament is called the ______.
questions.e: The Lok Sabha, or House of the People, is directly elected by voters.

questions.q: Which is the highest court of India?
questions.e: The Supreme Court in New Delhi is the apex court of the country.

questions.q: The reward earned by the owner of land when it is used in production is called ______.
questions.e: Land earns rent, labour wages, capital interest and entrepreneurship profit.

questions.q: The knowledge, skills and health of workers that make them productive are together called ______ capital.
questions.e: Human capital is built through education, training and healthcare.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution, guaranteeing the Right to Life, has been interpreted by courts to include the right to safe drinking water?
questions.e: Courts have held that the right to life under Article 21 includes access to safe water.

questions.t: Geography: Natural Resources and Their Use
questions.q: Coal, petroleum and natural gas, formed from remains of ancient plants and animals, are called ______.
questions.e: Fossil fuels formed over millions of years and are non-renewable.

questions.t: Geography: Natural Resources and Their Use
questions.q: The Chipko movement, in which villagers hugged trees to stop them being cut, began in the 1970s in which present-day state?
questions.e: The Chipko movement began in the Garhwal Himalayas of present-day Uttarakhand.

questions.q: Jute is called the 'golden fibre'. Which state is the largest producer of jute in India?
questions.e: The hot, humid Ganga-Brahmaputra delta of West Bengal is ideal for jute.

questions.q: Where did the Tatas set up India's first major iron and steel plant in 1907?
questions.e: TISCO was set up at Jamshedpur (then Sakchi) in 1907.

questions.q: Which Sultan of Delhi shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad in the Deccan?
questions.a: Muhammad bin Tughlaq|Muhammad Tughlaq|Muhammad bin Tughluq|Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq
questions.e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved his capital to Daulatabad but later returned to Delhi.

questions.q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by which two brothers?
questions.a: Harihara and Bukka|Bukka and Harihara|Harihara and Bukka Raya
questions.e: Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty founded Vijayanagara.

questions.t: History: The Rise of the Marathas
questions.q: The chief ministers who later became the real heads of Maratha power were called ______.
questions.e: From the early 18th century the Peshwas, based in Pune, led the Maratha state.

questions.t: History: The Colonial Era in India
questions.q: Which Portuguese sailor reached Calicut by sea in 1498?
questions.e: Vasco da Gama's voyage opened a direct sea route from Europe to India.

questions.t: Civics: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
questions.q: Which machine has replaced paper ballots for casting votes in Indian elections?
questions.e: EVMs record votes electronically; the VVPAT attached to them prints a slip for verification.

questions.t: Civics: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
questions.q: In which years were the first general elections of independent India held?
questions.e: The first general elections were held from October 1951 to February 1952.

questions.q: Who presides over the meetings of the Lok Sabha?
questions.a: Speaker|The Speaker|Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The Speaker, elected by Lok Sabha members, conducts its proceedings.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.e: The Vice-President of India chairs the Rajya Sabha.

questions.q: A case filed in court for the public good, even by a person not directly affected, is called ______.
questions.e: PIL lets any citizen approach the courts on behalf of those whose rights are violated.

questions.q: Tools, machines and buildings that are used in production for many years are called ______ capital.
questions.e: Fixed or physical capital is not used up in a single round of production.

questions.q: The person who brings together land, labour and capital and takes the risk of running a business is called an ______.
questions.e: An entrepreneur organises the other factors and bears the risk.

questions.q: Facilities such as water supply, sanitation, public hospitals and public transport, provided mainly by the government for everyone, are called ______.
questions.e: Public facilities meet basic needs and should be available to all.

questions.t: Geography: Natural Resources and Their Use
questions.q: Using resources to meet present needs while conserving them for future generations is called ______.
questions.e: Sustainable development balances today's needs with those of the future.

questions.q: Industries such as cotton textiles and sugar that get their raw materials from farms are called ______ industries.
questions.e: Agro-based industries process agricultural raw materials.

questions.q: Which Ahom general defeated the Mughal forces at the Battle of Saraighat in 1671?
questions.e: Lachit Borphukan led the Ahom navy and army to victory on the Brahmaputra at Saraighat.

questions.t: History: The Rise of the Marathas
questions.q: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was fought between the Marathas and which ruler?
questions.e: The Marathas were defeated at Panipat in 1761 by the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Abdali.

questions.t: History: The Colonial Era in India
questions.q: Which idea, argued by Dadabhai Naoroji, described how India's wealth was transferred to Britain under colonial rule?
questions.e: Naoroji's drain theory showed how taxes, salaries and profits flowed from India to Britain.

questions.t: Civics: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
questions.q: The option on an EVM that lets a voter reject all the candidates is called ______.
questions.e: NOTA, introduced in 2013, lets voters record that they reject all candidates.

questions.t: Civics: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
questions.q: In India, the candidate with the most votes in a constituency wins, even without a majority. This system is called ______.
questions.a: First past the post|First-past-the-post|FPTP|Simple majority system
questions.e: Under first-past-the-post, the highest vote-getter wins the seat.

questions.q: The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved. What fraction of its members retires every two years?
questions.e: One-third of Rajya Sabha members retire every two years, making it a permanent house.

questions.q: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to which house of Parliament?
questions.e: The government stays in office only while it has the confidence of the elected Lok Sabha.

questions.q: A baker's flour, sugar and the cash he keeps for daily expenses are examples of ______ capital.
questions.e: Working capital is used up in one cycle of production.

questions.q: A farmer rents land, hires workers and borrows money from a lender. Which reward does the lender receive?
questions.e: Interest is the reward paid for the use of borrowed capital.

questions.q: Public facilities are usually provided by the government because private companies mainly work for ______.
questions.e: Private firms seek profit, so they may not serve people who cannot pay.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of crop and cropping season is correctly matched?
questions.e: Wheat and mustard are rabi crops, while rice and cotton are kharif crops.

questions.t: History: The Rise of the Marathas
questions.q: Assertion (A): Shivaji built sea forts such as Sindhudurg and developed a navy. Reason (R): He wanted to protect the Konkan coast from the Siddis, the Portuguese and other sea powers.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R explains A
o: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: The navy and sea forts were meant to defend the coast, so R explains A.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly shows the order of courts from lowest to highest?
questions.a: District Court, High Court, Supreme Court
o: High Court, District Court, Supreme Court
Supreme Court, High Court, District Court
District Court, Supreme Court, High Court
questions.e: India has an integrated judiciary with appeals from district courts to high courts to the Supreme Court.

questions.t: Geography: Natural Resources and Their Use
questions.q: Data: A town's electricity comes from coal 55%, hydropower 15%, solar 20% and wind 10%.
p: (a) What percentage of the town's electricity comes from renewable sources?
(b) Which of the listed sources is non-renewable?
Coal
questions.e: Hydro, solar and wind add up to 15 + 20 + 10 = 45%; coal is a non-renewable fossil fuel.

questions.q: The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526 and the Battle of Haldighati in 1576.
p: (a) How many years apart were these two battles?
years
(b) Which ruler of Mewar fought the Mughal army at Haldighati?
Maharana Pratap|Rana Pratap|Pratap Singh
(c) Who was the Mughal emperor at the time of Haldighati?
Akbar
questions.e: 1576 - 1526 = 50; Maharana Pratap faced Akbar's forces at Haldighati.

questions.t: History: The Colonial Era in India
questions.q: The English East India Company was founded in 1600. After winning the Battle of Buxar in 1764, it received the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha in 1765.
p: (a) How many years after its founding did the Company get the Diwani?
years
(b) What right did the Diwani give the Company?
Collect revenue|Revenue collection|Collect land revenue|Collect taxes|Tax collection
questions.e: 1765 - 1600 = 165; the Diwani gave the Company the right to collect land revenue.

questions.t: Civics: Universal Franchise and India's Electoral System
questions.q: Data: In a constituency, 2,00,000 voters were registered and 1,30,000 voted. Asha got 55,000 votes, Bina 45,000 and Chetan 30,000.
p: (a) What was the voter turnout?
(b) Who won the election?
Asha
(c) Did the winner get more than half of the votes polled? (Yes/No)
No
questions.e: Turnout = 130000 ÷ 200000 = 65%; Asha won with about 42% of votes, showing how first-past-the-post works.

questions.q: Data: Ravi's bakery in one year — sales ₹5,00,000; rent ₹60,000; wages ₹1,80,000; interest ₹20,000; raw materials ₹1,40,000.
p: (a) What were the total costs?
(b) What was Ravi's profit?
(c) Profit is the reward for which factor of production?
Entrepreneurship|Entrepreneur|Enterprise
questions.e: Costs = 60000 + 180000 + 20000 + 140000 = ₹4,00,000, so profit = ₹1,00,000, the entrepreneur's reward.

questions.q: On which date was the Bastille stormed in Paris?
questions.e: The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 marks the start of the French Revolution.

questions.t: History: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution
questions.q: Who led the Bolshevik Party during the October Revolution of 1917?
questions.e: Lenin led the Bolsheviks to seize power in October 1917.

questions.t: History: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: On which date did Hitler become Chancellor of Germany?
questions.e: President Hindenburg appointed Hitler Chancellor on 30 January 1933.

questions.q: The northernmost and highest range of the Himalayas is called the ______.
questions.e: The Himadri contains the highest peaks, with an average height of about 6,000 m.

questions.q: The Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet to form the Ganga at which place?
questions.e: The two headstreams join at Devprayag in Uttarakhand.

questions.q: Which place in Meghalaya receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world?
questions.e: Mawsynram, on the southern Khasi hills, receives the world's highest average rainfall.

questions.t: Civics: What is Democracy? Why Democracy?
questions.q: Abraham Lincoln defined democracy as government of the people, by the people and ______ the people.
questions.e: Lincoln's definition stresses that democracy exists for the benefit of the people.

questions.q: Who led the struggle against apartheid and became South Africa's first black President?
questions.e: Nelson Mandela became President in 1994 after South Africa's first democratic elections.

questions.q: Which Fundamental Right did Dr Ambedkar call the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.e: It lets citizens go to the courts to enforce all other Fundamental Rights.

questions.t: Economics: The Story of Village Palampur
questions.q: The standard unit for measuring land area used in the Palampur story is the ______.
questions.e: A hectare is the area of a square with 100-metre sides.

questions.q: When more people work on a farm than needed and removing some would not reduce output, it is called ______ unemployment.
questions.e: In disguised unemployment, people appear employed but add nothing to output.

questions.q: Unemployment among educated youth who cannot find jobs matching their qualifications is called ______ unemployment.
questions.e: Educated unemployment is common in urban areas.

questions.q: In India, the calorie requirement used to estimate the rural poverty line was how many calories per person per day?
questions.e: The rural norm was 2400 calories and the urban norm 2100 calories per person per day.

questions.q: A person whose income or consumption falls below the minimum level needed to meet basic needs is said to be below the ______.
questions.e: The poverty line is the minimum level of income or consumption for basic needs.

questions.q: Which tax, paid to the Church by peasants, was one-tenth of their agricultural produce?
questions.e: The tithe was a church tax of about one-tenth of produce.

questions.q: Which philosopher proposed the separation of powers among the legislature, executive and judiciary in 'The Spirit of the Laws'?
questions.e: Montesquieu argued that dividing power prevents tyranny.

questions.t: History: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution
questions.q: The elected consultative parliament created by the Tsar after the 1905 Revolution was called the ______.
questions.e: Tsar Nicholas II allowed an elected Duma after 1905 but often dismissed it.

questions.t: History: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Which law of March 1933 established dictatorship in Germany by giving Hitler power to rule by decree?
questions.e: The Enabling Act let Hitler sideline Parliament and rule by decree.

questions.q: Longitudinal valleys between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks, such as Dehradun, are called ______.
questions.e: Duns like Dehradun, Kotli Dun and Patli Dun lie between the Himachal and the Shiwaliks.

questions.q: Which is the highest peak of peninsular India?
questions.e: Anai Mudi (2,695 m) in the Western Ghats is the highest peak of the peninsula.

questions.q: Which two west-flowing peninsular rivers flow through rift valleys?
questions.a: Narmada and Tapi|Narmada and Tapti|Tapi and Narmada|Tapti and Narmada
questions.e: The Narmada and Tapi flow westward through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea.

questions.q: Pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka that help the early ripening of mangoes are called ______.
questions.e: Mango showers fall towards the end of summer, just before the monsoon.

questions.t: Civics: What is Democracy? Why Democracy?
questions.q: In which country did the PRI party win every election from 1930 to 2000, so elections were not truly free?
questions.e: In Mexico the PRI used unfair means to win, so voters had no real choice.

questions.q: On which island prison was Nelson Mandela held for most of his 28 years in jail?
questions.e: Mandela spent most of his imprisonment on Robben Island.

questions.q: Who moved the 'Objectives Resolution' in the Constituent Assembly in 1946?
questions.e: Nehru's Objectives Resolution later shaped the Preamble.

questions.q: In 1928, which leader, along with eight other Congress leaders, drafted a constitution for India?
questions.e: The Nehru Report of 1928 was drafted under Motilal Nehru.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution abolished untouchability?
questions.e: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes its practice punishable.

questions.t: Economics: The Story of Village Palampur
questions.q: Growing more than one crop on the same piece of land during a year is called ______.
questions.e: Multiple cropping is the most common way of raising production on a fixed amount of land.

questions.q: Unemployment that occurs when people cannot find work during some months of the year, common in farming, is called ______ unemployment.
questions.e: Farm work is busy at sowing and harvesting time but scarce in other months.

questions.q: Which law of 2005 guarantees 100 days of wage employment in a year to rural households?
questions.a: MGNREGA|NREGA|MGNREGS|Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act|National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
questions.e: The NREGA of 2005, later renamed MGNREGA, gives rural households a legal right to work.

questions.q: Members of the Third Estate declared themselves a National Assembly and swore not to disperse until France had a constitution. Where did they take this oath?
questions.a: Indoor tennis court|Tennis court|Tennis Court at Versailles
questions.e: This was the Tennis Court Oath of 20 June 1789 at Versailles.

questions.t: History: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution
questions.q: Under Stalin's collectivisation, well-to-do peasants accused of hoarding grain were targeted. What were they called?
questions.e: Stalin blamed the kulaks for grain shortages and sought to eliminate them.

questions.t: History: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Hitler's idea of 'living space', used to justify conquering territory in the east, was called ______.
questions.e: Lebensraum meant acquiring new territories for German settlement.

questions.q: In the northern plains, the newer, younger alluvial deposits of the flood plains are called ______.
questions.e: Khadar is renewed almost every year by floods, unlike older bhangar.

questions.q: Why do the Narmada and Tapi form estuaries and not deltas? Because they flow through hard rock and carry little ______.
questions.e: Fast-flowing rivers over hard rock carry little silt, so they form estuaries.

questions.q: During winter, north-western India receives light rain from cyclonic systems coming from the Mediterranean region. These are called ______.
questions.e: This winter rain is important for the rabi crops of north-west India.

questions.t: Civics: What is Democracy? Why Democracy?
questions.q: The principle 'one person, one vote, one value' is a feature of which kind of franchise?
questions.a: Universal adult franchise|Universal adult suffrage|Universal franchise
questions.e: Universal adult franchise gives every adult an equal vote.

questions.q: How many members did India's Constituent Assembly have after Partition?
questions.e: The Assembly had 389 members before Partition and 299 after it.

questions.q: Which independent body, set up in 1993, investigates complaints of human rights violations in India?
questions.e: The NHRC focuses on helping victims secure their human rights.

questions.t: Economics: The Story of Village Palampur
questions.q: The use of HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers and irrigation from the late 1960s, which raised wheat and rice output mainly in Punjab, Haryana and western UP, is called the ______.
questions.e: The Green Revolution greatly increased foodgrain production in irrigated regions.

questions.q: In the NCERT story, which of the two boys, Sakal or Vilas, studied and trained in computers and got a good job?
questions.e: Investment in Sakal's education and health made him a productive human resource.

questions.q: When the poor are forced to live only among the poor and are denied equal access to better facilities, it is called social ______.
questions.e: Social exclusion can be both a cause and a result of poverty.

questions.t: History: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution
questions.q: Assertion (A): The Provisional Government in Russia lost popular support during 1917. Reason (R): It kept Russia in the First World War and delayed land reform.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R explains A
o: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: War losses and unmet demand for land turned people towards the Bolsheviks, so R explains A.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches a lake with its type?
questions.e: Chilika is a lagoon, Sambhar is a salt lake and Wular is a freshwater lake.

questions.t: Civics: What is Democracy? Why Democracy?
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of democracy?
questions.a: Rulers cannot be changed by the people
questions.e: In a democracy, people must have the choice and opportunity to change their rulers.

questions.q: In 1789, Louis XVI called a meeting of the Estates General to approve new taxes. Traditionally, each estate had one vote.
p: (a) Which estate demanded that voting be by each member instead of by estate?
Third Estate|The Third Estate
(b) Which Jacobin leader led the period of severe control and punishment known as the Reign of Terror (1793–94)?
Robespierre|Maximilian Robespierre|Maximilien Robespierre
questions.e: The Third Estate wanted one member, one vote; Robespierre led the Reign of Terror.

questions.t: History: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
questions.q: Germany's Weimar Republic was weakened by the harsh Treaty of Versailles (1919), hyperinflation in 1923 and the Great Depression that began in 1929.
p: (a) In which city did the 1929 stock market crash that triggered the Depression take place?
New York|New York City|Wall Street
(b) How many years after the Treaty of Versailles did the Great Depression begin?
years
(c) The Nazi genocide of Jews is known as the ______.
Holocaust|The Holocaust|Shoah
questions.e: The Wall Street crash of 1929 came 10 years after Versailles; the Nazis later carried out the Holocaust.

questions.q: Data: The average monthly temperature of a place is 14°C in January and 33°C in May. Its annual rainfall is 70 cm, mostly from June to September.
p: (a) What is the annual range of temperature?
°C
(b) In which season does the place get most of its rain?
Rainy season|Monsoon|Monsoon season|Southwest monsoon|Summer monsoon
questions.e: 33 - 14 = 19°C; June–September rain comes from the south-west monsoon.

questions.q: Case: Ravi, aged 12, works in a fireworks factory. Meena is denied entry to a public temple because of her caste.
p: (a) Which Fundamental Right is violated in Ravi's case?
Right against Exploitation
(b) Which Fundamental Right protects Meena from discrimination?
Right to Equality
(c) Children below what age cannot be employed in factories, mines or hazardous work?
years
questions.e: Child labour in hazardous work violates the Right against Exploitation; caste discrimination violates the Right to Equality.

questions.t: Economics: The Story of Village Palampur
questions.q: Data: Palampur has about 450 families. 150 are landless; 240 are small farmers with less than 2 hectares; 60 are medium and large farmers with more than 2 hectares.
p: (a) How many families own some land?
families
(b) What percentage of all families are small farmers (to the nearest whole number)?
questions.e: 240 + 60 = 300 own land; 240 ÷ 450 ≈ 53%, showing unequal land distribution.

questions.t: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.q: Who founded the secret society 'Young Italy' in 1831?
questions.e: Mazzini founded Young Italy to work for a unified Italian republic.

questions.q: In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place in Amritsar?
questions.e: General Dyer's troops fired on a peaceful crowd on 13 April 1919.

questions.q: Gandhiji's Salt March began at Sabarmati Ashram and ended at which coastal village?
questions.e: Gandhiji broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.

questions.t: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: Who developed the first known printing press in Europe in the 1430s?
questions.e: Gutenberg's press, developed in Strasbourg, used movable metal type.

questions.q: The 1992 Earth Summit, which adopted Agenda 21, was held in which city?
questions.e: The Rio Earth Summit focused on environmental protection and sustainable development.

questions.q: The 'slash and burn' type of farming practised in the north-eastern states is called ______.
questions.e: In jhumming, a patch of forest is cleared and burnt, farmed for a few years and then left fallow.

questions.q: Lignite, a low-grade brown coal, is mined mainly at which place in Tamil Nadu?
questions.e: Neyveli has India's major lignite reserves, used to generate electricity.

questions.q: In Belgium, the majority community in the Flemish region speaks which language?
questions.e: About 59% of Belgians, mostly in Flanders, speak Dutch.

questions.q: Subjects such as education, forests, trade unions, marriage and adoption are included in which list?
questions.e: Both the Union and the states can make laws on Concurrent List subjects.

questions.q: A system in which only one party is allowed to control and run the government, as in China, is called a ______ system.
questions.e: In a one-party system, voters have no real choice between parties.

questions.q: The total income of a country divided by its total population is called ______.
questions.e: Per capita income is commonly used to compare countries.

questions.t: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.q: Goods used up in producing final goods, such as wheat used by a flour mill, are called ______ goods.
questions.e: Only final goods are counted in GDP to avoid double counting intermediate goods.

questions.q: Assets such as land, buildings or livestock that a borrower pledges as a guarantee to a lender are called ______.
questions.e: The lender can sell the collateral if the loan is not repaid.

questions.q: Who founded the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006?
questions.e: Muhammad Yunus pioneered small loans to poor rural borrowers, mostly women.

questions.t: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.q: Which Prussian chief minister was the architect of German unification?
questions.e: Bismarck unified Germany through three wars, completing it in 1871.

questions.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn in February 1922 after a violent clash at which place?
questions.e: Gandhiji called off the movement after a mob burnt a police station at Chauri Chaura.

questions.t: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: Who wrote the 'Ninety-Five Theses' criticising practices of the Roman Catholic Church in 1517?
questions.e: Printed copies of Luther's theses spread quickly and led to the Protestant Reformation.

questions.q: Black soil, ideal for growing cotton, is also called ______ soil.
questions.e: Black or regur soil retains moisture well and is found on the Deccan trap.

questions.q: Ploughing along the contour lines of a slope to slow down the flow of water is called ______.
questions.e: Contour ploughing reduces soil erosion on hill slopes.

questions.q: Crops like watermelon, muskmelon and cucumber grown in the short season between rabi and kharif are called ______ crops.
questions.e: Zaid crops are grown in the short summer season.

questions.q: Which state is the largest producer of tea in India?
questions.e: Assam's warm, moist climate and well-drained hill slopes suit tea.

questions.q: Which ore is the main raw material for making aluminium?
questions.e: Aluminium is obtained from bauxite; Odisha is the largest producer.

questions.q: In which country did majoritarian policies lead to a civil war after Tamil groups demanded a separate state?
questions.e: Sri Lanka's Sinhala-first policies alienated Sri Lankan Tamils and led to civil war.

questions.q: Federations like India, Spain and Belgium, where a large country divides its power between the centre and the states, are called ______ federations.
questions.e: In holding-together federations, the central government tends to be more powerful.

questions.q: Which body recognises political parties as national or state parties in India?
questions.e: The Election Commission recognises parties based on their vote share and seats.

questions.q: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report?
questions.e: The UNDP ranks countries by the Human Development Index.

questions.t: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.q: Enterprises with regular terms of employment that are registered with the government and follow its rules form the ______ sector.
questions.e: Organised sector workers enjoy job security and benefits.

questions.t: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.q: In which sector does the government own most of the assets and provide services, such as Indian Railways?
questions.e: Indian Railways and Post Offices are public sector enterprises.

questions.q: Deposits in bank accounts that can be withdrawn whenever the account holder wants are called ______ deposits.
questions.e: Demand deposits can be withdrawn on demand and are used for cheque payments.

questions.q: Which institution supervises the functioning of formal sources of loans in India?
questions.e: The RBI monitors how banks maintain cash balances and give loans.

questions.t: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.q: The customs union formed in 1834 at Prussia's initiative, which abolished tariff barriers among German states, was called the ______.
questions.e: The Zollverein created a unified economic territory that aided German nationalism.

questions.q: At its Lahore session in December 1929, under Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress formalised which demand?
questions.e: The Lahore Congress demanded Purna Swaraj, and 26 January 1930 was celebrated as Independence Day.

questions.t: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: Which 1878 law gave the colonial government powers to censor reports and editorials in Indian-language newspapers?
questions.e: The Vernacular Press Act was modelled on the Irish Press Laws.

questions.q: Land made unfit for cultivation by deep gullies, as in the Chambal basin, is called ______.
questions.e: Running water cuts deep channels, turning land into bad land or ravines.

questions.q: The monazite sands of Kerala are rich in which nuclear mineral?
questions.e: Kerala's monazite sands are an important source of thorium.

questions.q: Power shared among the legislature, executive and judiciary is called ______ distribution of power.
questions.e: Organs at the same level share power horizontally and check one another.

questions.q: Subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists, like computer software, are called ______ subjects.
questions.e: The Union government has the power to legislate on residuary subjects.

questions.q: Under the 1992 constitutional amendment, at least what fraction of seats in local government bodies is reserved for women?
questions.e: The 73rd and 74th Amendments reserve at least one-third of seats for women.

questions.q: Which law prevents elected MPs and MLAs from changing parties after an election?
questions.e: Under the anti-defection law, a legislator who changes party loses the seat.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why Kerala has a low infant mortality rate despite not having the highest per capita income?
questions.a: Adequate basic health and educational facilities
o: Highest per capita income in India
questions.e: Kerala's public health and education facilities reduce infant deaths, showing that income alone does not measure development.

questions.t: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.q: Which sector contributes the largest share to India's GDP today?
questions.e: The tertiary sector became the largest producing sector, replacing the primary sector.

questions.q: A farmer borrows from a moneylender at high interest, his crop fails and he must sell part of his land to repay. This situation is called a ______.
questions.e: When repayment becomes impossible, credit pushes the borrower into a debt trap.

questions.q: Arrange these events in chronological order.
questions.a: Champaran, Rowlatt Satyagraha, Non-Cooperation, Salt March
o: Rowlatt Satyagraha, Champaran, Non-Cooperation, Salt March
Champaran, Non-Cooperation, Rowlatt Satyagraha, Salt March
Non-Cooperation, Champaran, Salt March, Rowlatt Satyagraha
questions.e: Champaran (1917), Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919), Non-Cooperation (1920–22) and the Salt March (1930).

questions.q: Assertion (A): Rice is grown in Punjab and Haryana even though they receive low rainfall. Reason (R): Canal irrigation and tubewells have made rice cultivation possible there.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R explains A
o: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.e: Irrigation makes rice possible in these low-rainfall areas, so R explains A.

questions.q: Which of the following countries is generally described as having a two-party system?
questions.e: In the USA, power usually alternates between two main parties.

questions.t: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.q: In 1815, European powers met at Vienna under the Austrian Chancellor Metternich. Later, in 1832, the Treaty of Constantinople recognised Greece as an independent nation.
p: (a) What was the main aim of the Treaty of Vienna?
Restore monarchies|Restore the monarchies|Undo Napoleonic changes|Restore conservative regimes|Undo Napoleon's changes
(b) How many years after the Congress of Vienna was Greece recognised as independent?
years
(c) Greece had been part of which empire before independence?
Ottoman Empire|Ottoman|Ottomans|Turkish Empire
questions.e: Vienna (1815) tried to undo Napoleon's changes; Greece won independence from the Ottomans in 1832, 17 years later.

questions.t: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: Gutenberg printed about 180 copies of the Bible, and it took about three years to produce them. Before this, a single handwritten copy could take a scribe years.
p: (a) On average, how many copies were produced per year?
copies
(b) Which earlier method of printing, using carved wooden blocks, was developed in China?
Woodblock printing|Woodblock|Block printing|Hand printing
questions.e: 180 ÷ 3 = 60 copies a year, far faster than copying by hand; China had earlier used woodblock printing.

questions.q: Data: Magnetite contains up to 70% iron; haematite contains 50–60% iron.
p: (a) Which is the finest iron ore?
Magnetite
(b) At most, how much iron can be obtained from 1,000 kg of magnetite with 70% iron?
kg
(c) Which iron ore mine in Karnataka was a 100% export unit?
Kudremukh
questions.e: Magnetite is the finest ore; 70% of 1,000 kg = 700 kg; Kudremukh exported its ore.

questions.q: Data: Belgium — Dutch speakers 59%, French speakers 40%, German speakers 1%. In the capital Brussels, about 80% speak French and 20% Dutch.
p: (a) Which group is a minority in the country but a majority in Brussels?
French speakers|French|French-speaking
(b) Belgium created a special government elected by people of one language community. What is it called?
Community government|Community
questions.e: Belgium's accommodation, including community government, prevented conflict between its language groups.

questions.q: Data: Monthly incomes of five citizens. Country A: 9500, 10500, 9800, 10000, 10200. Country B: 500, 500, 500, 500, 48000.
p: (a) What is the average income in Country A?
(b) What is the average income in Country B?
(c) In which country is income more equally distributed?
Country A
questions.e: Both averages are 10000, but averages hide inequality: in Country B one person earns almost everything.
